title: rate-policy-mirroring-gap-during-geo-fence-failover
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: During a simulated geo-region failover we observed a window where per-org and per-route rate policies were inconsistently applied between the primary and standby policy mirrors. Traffic routed into the standby region experienced silent allowance for burst credits on a subset of routes, resulting in chargeable usage being unmetered for ~7 minutes for impacted customers. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a hardening rollout to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: Provision two edge regions: eu-west-1 (primary) and eu-central-1 (standby) with policy-mirroring enabled
Create org O123 with per-route burst policy: /generate -> 100 burst credits, 10/s sustained
Start steady traffic from test harness pinned to primary; confirm policy counters increment and billing meters update
Trigger controlled failover by disabling primary control-plane connectivity for 30s
Observe incoming requests routed to standby: some requests bypass burst accounting for route /generate for ~5-8 minutes
Collect policy-sync logs, edge-meter snapshots, and route metadata during the failover window
timeline_summary: 2026-02-10: Issue reported by Platform SRE during chaos experiment
2026-02-11: Initial triage: reproduced in lab; traffic allowed without burst decrement
2026-02-15: Root-cause hypothesis formed (policy mirror_apply race on incremental patches)
2026-02-18: Hotfix deployed to standby: conservative-deny fallback while policy mirror stale
2026-03-01: Integration tests added to failover harness
2026-03-12: Preparing durable fix and monitoring dashboards for rollout
observed_behavior: Standby region accepted requests and served generated responses while the per-route burst credit counters on the central billing aggregator remained stale; downstream metering pipeline received delayed usage batches causing a temporary undercount and silent allowance beyond allocated burst.
expected_behavior: During regional failover the standby control-plane should atomically apply the latest policy snapshot or apply a conservative fallback (deny/exhaustive-accounting) until consistent mirroring is confirmed. Metering should not drop or defer chargeable tokens without explicit deprecation windows.
root_cause: Race condition in the policy-mirror controller where incremental patch application (CRDT-style deltas) on standby could be partially applied while the route-to-credit mapping used by the local enforcer still referenced older in-memory schemas. The enforcer evaluated the route as "allow-with-burst" because the local transient state lacked the latest decrement offsets, while the central meter aggregator did not receive the per-token debit due to batching being queued and later deduplicated incorrectly.
mitigation_applied: Hotfix: standby control-plane now applies policy snapshots atomically; a temporary conservative-fallback flag enforces 'no-burst' until mirror acked
Backfilled charges for affected window from buffered per-edge logs and reconciled into billing system
Rate-limit gating added: standby will limit to sustained-rate if mirror age > 2s
detailed_fix_proposal: Replace incremental delta-apply path with transactional apply-and-ack semantics for mirror updates
Introduce policy version vector and per-route apply checkpoints to ensure enforcer cannot evaluate new traffic until all dependent counters are reconciled
Add idempotent meter ingestion tags (mirror_origin, apply_version) so late-arriving usage is not deduped incorrectly
Extend integration test harness to simulate partial-patch delivery and verify conservative fallback behavior
acceptance_criteria: Failover experiment shows no silent allowance across 1000 simulated orgs and 10k routes
Bench: standby mirror-apply adds <5ms median overhead and no measurable throughput regression
New e2e tests pass in CI with flakiness <1% over 500 runs
Monitoring alert fires if policy-mirror age > 2s and disabled auto-allow
qa_and_tests: Unit tests for transactional apply path (existing delta tests retired)
Chaos test: random delay and reorder of mirror packets between control-plane replicas
Billing reconciliation test: inject synthetic usage and verify backfill produces exact charge reconciliation
Canary rollout to eu-central-1 with synthetic traffic gating
rollout_plan: Canary deploy fix to standby eu-central-1 edges (50 hosts) -> monitor for 24h
Gradual rollout to other standby regions over 48h with automated rollback on error budget hit
Post-deploy audit: reconcile last 72h of meter batches and visually verify no undercount windows
monitoring_and_alerting_changes: Dashboard panels: per-route burst-decrement-rate vs aggregate meter-ingest-rate to detect divergence
next_steps: Merge PR #589 and #311, run extended CI (48h flake detection)
Schedule canary tomorrow 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC with SRE present
Notify account teams for customers in eu region and prepare communication if any billing corrections required
